method: Direct header/implementation/class-test audit at the pinned revision; no C++ was built or executed. Packaged fixtures are exact source bytes; every other expectation is either a transcribed class-test literal or a natively derived guard, and the two are kept apart below.

source_files.role: Ported in full. 39 public function names in 40 overloads, the nested TempDir (two constructors, destructor, deleted copy/move, getPath), CopyOptions and MatchingFileListsStatus, plus the private helpers observable through them. Every member is listed in the support document's API table.

Ported in full: filesystem operations, lexical path helpers, permission probes, wildcard listing, resource lookup and the shared-data resolution order. Its platform branches (Windows.h, Shlwapi.h, dlfcn.h, mach-o/dyld.h) are replaced by portable std::fs/std::path; the dladdr library-directory probe becomes an explicit FileContext candidate.

Ported in full: OpenMS.ini policy, temporary/user/home/config directory resolution and findDatabase. Kept in a separate translation unit upstream so Param and ParamXMLFile stay out of File.cpp; here the equivalent split is the paramxml cargo feature.

Ported in full: TempDir, getTemporaryFile and the temporary-file registry. The exit-time TemporaryFiles_ registry of uncreated names is replaced by owned TempFile/TempDir guards; mkdtemp's _XXXXXX becomes an exclusive create with the source's own 100-attempt retry cap.
Not re-ported here; File::basename delegates to PathUtils::basename, which src/system/path_utils.rs already covers. Hashed because File's basename/stemName/extension results are defined by it.

Not re-ported here. File::stemName and File::extension are defined in terms of FileNameUtils::stripExtension, which crate::format::file_types::strip_extension provides; hashed because the compound-extension literals in the class test come from it.
As above: the implementation that decides where stemName cuts, including the known-compound-extension table and the last-dot fallback for an unknown one.

Not ported for this group. Read to establish what getUniqueName's date and time actually are before the '-' and ':' are stripped, and therefore that the port's switch to UTC is a stated divergence rather than an accident.
Oracle: 35 START_SECTIONs, all mapped in tests/system_file.rs. Also the origin of the two packaged fixtures and of the writable() path-depth sweep and concurrency regressions.
Not ported. Read for the shared-data resolution contract the SDK checks separately from File_test.cpp, confirming that the marker file and the override precedence are the whole of isOpenMSDataPath_.

Not ported: it is a CMake template whose substituted values are build-machine paths. Read to establish exactly which of resolveOpenMSDataPath_'s candidates are compiled in, and therefore which ones become explicit FileContext::data_candidates entries.

source_anchors.operation: TempDir's destructor removes the tree unless keep_dir was set at construction; it returns nothing and throws nothing, so a failed removal is already silent in the source. The port's Drop is silent for the same reason and offers close() to make it visible.

listDirectories documents 'an empty list on any error or if the path is not a directory (no throw)', so a caller cannot tell an unreadable directory from an empty one; the port returns the error instead
getUserDirectory's documentation names OPENMS_HOME_DIR, and getSystemParameters' at line 283 repeats it, but FileConfig.cpp reads OPENMS_HOME_PATH; the implementation is what the port follows
findExecutable does not require the file to have executable permission set, and says so; existence and not-a-directory are the whole test
empty() returns true when the path is missing, when file_size reports an error (which it does for a directory) and when the size is zero, so it reads as 'not a nonempty regular file'

getModificationTime uses stat()'s st_mtime rather than std::filesystem::last_write_time, because file_time_type's epoch is implementation-defined (2174 on libstdc++, 1601 on MSVC) and clock_cast is unavailable on the supported toolchains; -1 is both the failure sentinel and a legitimate time one second before the epoch
fileSize returns -1 from a UInt64 function, so a missing file reaches the caller as 18446744073709551615 and compares greater than every real size; the port returns Result<u64>

rename resolves both paths with canonical() and returns true unchanged when they are the same file; with overwrite_existing it removes the destination *before* renaming, so a rename that then fails leaves the caller with neither file; the EXDEV branch copies and removes, preserving what Qt's QFile::rename did silently
remove() is std::remove, which on POSIX unlinks a file and also removes an empty directory, and treats an absent path as success
removeDir is fs::remove_all, identical to removeDirRecursively at line 386 despite the name and the header's 'and all its contents' wording; both print to stderr and return false on failure
absolutePath returns fs::current_path() for an empty input and is otherwise fs::absolute, which is purely lexical: '..' is not collapsed and symlinks are not resolved
path() returns "." rather than an empty string for a bare filename, with the comment explaining that path(f) + '/' + basename(f) would otherwise turn a relative name into an absolute one

writable() is a query that must not change the answer: it probes an absent path with a file of its own rather than with the caller's name, retries on EEXIST, and falls back to access(dir, W_OK) when the create fails for a reason about the probe *name* (ENAMETOOLONG, or the ENOENT/EINVAL the Windows CRT folds ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE onto). The port reproduces the fallback with progressively shorter probe names, because safe Rust has no access(2) and io::ErrorKind::InvalidFilename is unstable at the crate's minimum Rust version

find() returns an already existing input unchanged, throws for an empty or whitespace-only name because prefixing a directory would otherwise 'find' the directory, pushes the data path last so caller directories win, appends File::path(filename) to every directory (which is "." and not empty for a bare name), and builds a failure hint naming the resolved data path and OPENMS_DATA_PATH

fileList matches with POSIX fnmatch (flags 0) or Windows PathMatchSpecA, considers only regular files, sorts, and returns whether the output is nonempty; fnmatch operates on bytes, so '?' there covers one byte where the port's character-based matcher covers one character

getUniqueName is DateTime::now()'s local date and time with '-' and ':' removed, an optional gethostname, the pid, and a static atomic counter whose first emitted value is 1; the port uses UTC and the HOSTNAME/COMPUTERNAME environment variable, so the host part may legitimately be absent

resolveOpenMSDataPath_ order: OPENMS_DATA_PATH is authoritative and an invalid override fails instead of falling through; otherwise the dladdr library directory, the executable directory, the macOS bundle, then the two compiled-in paths. Only success is cached, in a thread-safe function-local static
isOpenMSDataPath_ is exactly exists(path + "/CHEMISTRY/unimod.xml"); the port uses the same marker and the crate's packaged chemistry tables deliberately do not satisfy it

findSiblingTOPPExecutable searches the executable directory and three macOS bundle alternatives only, carries a TODO about probing PATH, and throws FileNotFound otherwise; the class test pins the siblings-only contract
validateMatchingFileNames compares two std::sets, so multiplicity is discarded: two equal-length lists with the same set but different multiplicities are ORDER_MISMATCH rather than SET_MISMATCH

getTempDirectory calls getSystemParameters() as its first statement, before it even looks at OPENMS_TMPDIR, so a malformed OpenMS.ini is an error even when the environment override would have answered; getUserDirectory at line 48 does the same
getUserDirectory reads OPENMS_HOME_PATH (not the header's OPENMS_HOME_DIR) and finishes with ensureLastChar(dir, '/'), which turns an explicitly empty configured value into the filesystem root

getOpenMSConfigDir switches on __unix__, which Apple's compilers do not define, so macOS takes the <home>/.OpenMS branch and never consults XDG_CONFIG_HOME; the port switches on cfg!(all(unix, not(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "ios")))) rather than on Rust's unix flag, which is set on macOS

getSystemParameters builds p_new from the defaults, updates it with the file's tree, and then returns p rather than p_new, discarding the repair; the only observable effect is that version has been overwritten in the returned tree, and no file is rewritten

createUniqueDir_ caps its retry at 100 attempts on Windows and relies on mkdtemp's _XXXXXX elsewhere; both create the parent chain first, because only the leaf is created otherwise. The port keeps the 100-attempt cap for both the directory and the file guard

the no-argument TempDir uses the prefix getTempDirectory() + "/" + getUniqueName(), while the two-argument one at line 133 prefixes OpenMSTempDir_; the two constructors therefore produce differently shaped names, and the port uses the second shape for both
~TempDir logs at debug level and returns when keep_dir_ is set, otherwise calls removeDirRecursively and discards its bool; no exception escapes the destructor

getTemporaryFile returns a nonempty alternative_file untouched and unregistered; otherwise it returns a name that is never created, only queued for deletion at exit by TemporaryFiles_::~TemporaryFiles_ at line 179

evidence.description: Tier 3 is the transcription of File_test.cpp's literals, section by section, with the source section named above each Rust test. Tier 4 covers the natively derived guards: concurrency (probe and no-clobber publication), lifecycle (guard drop, keep, close), symbolic-link and encoding boundaries, the resource ceilings, and the two expectations derived from the platform rather than from a literal — the __unix__ configuration-directory branch, and the writable() path-depth sweep, which compares against the operating system's own answer instead of a hard-coded length. No retained C++ output and no oracle driver exists for File, whose answers are properties of the machine rather than of a fixture, so no tier 1 or tier 2 claim is made.

not_reproducible_literally: makeDir (File_test.cpp:459) additionally changes the process working directory to test a relative path. No test in a multithreaded binary may do that, so the port checks the absolute chain, idempotence on an existing directory, and the occupied-path and depth-ceiling failures instead.

getUniqueName (File_test.cpp:375) asserts that the hostname form is strictly longer than the no-hostname form. The port reads HOSTNAME rather than calling gethostname, and that variable is normally unset for a non-interactive process, so the host part may legitimately be absent; the section's other literal, split.size() >= 4, is reproduced exactly.

getOpenMSConfigDir (File_test.cpp:501) sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME with setenv. FileContext::from_environment reads it once instead of on every call, so the port asserts on the isolated context's branch, suffix and absent trailing separator.

findDoc (File_test.cpp:267) is guarded by ENABLE_DOCS and resolves files from the upstream source and build trees, which do not exist here; the port exercises the same search through explicit documentation directories.

independently_derived: A file stamped half a second before the Unix epoch must report -1, not 0, because POSIX st_mtim.tv_sec truncates towards negative infinity; this follows from the stat() contract the source cites and not from any class-test literal.

writable() must agree with the operating system at every path depth. The test establishes ground truth by actually creating the file, so it needs no platform path limit to be hard-coded; without the short-name probe fallback it fails on Linux, which is how the gap was found.

extension() cuts the basename at the stem's length, and the stem is a prefix of the basename, so that offset is always a character boundary; dir/<multi-byte>.txt therefore cannot panic, and the test pins it for a three-character Japanese name.
Exactly one of several concurrent no-clobber movers can win, because publication is a hard link: the winner's destination holds one input's bytes in full and every loser's input is still present.
Two simultaneous writable() probes of the same absent path must both answer true and must leave a concurrent writer's output intact, since neither probe ever touches the queried name.
A directory-link cycle inside a recursive copy is detected from the canonical ancestor set, so the traversal terminates for input the source would follow indefinitely.

native_adaptations: Explicit FileContext replaces automatic dladdr library-address discovery, compiled-in checkout paths and process-global environment reads; the source's success-only caching and retry-after-correction policy is preserved, and clear_data_cache is added because a function-local static cannot offer it.

Owned TempFile/TempDir guards replace the process-exit filename registry; the default TempFile reserves a real file exclusively rather than returning an uncreated name. Drop is silent, as the source's destructor is; close() reports.

Regular-file no-clobber publication uses hard links, so unsupported filesystems, no-clobber directory/symlink moves and cross-device directory/symlink moves are checked errors rather than racy emulation.

Overwrite moves do not pre-delete the destination, correcting the source's delete-then-rename window. Directory copy preflights cycles, self/descendant copies, all visible Cancel conflicts and destination directory symlinks.

Permission queries are effective-process semantic probes rather than real-uid access(2) or Windows ACL calculations; FIFOs and devices are never opened, and the requested basename is never created. The source's name-length fallback is reproduced with shorter probe names.
Portable character-based Unicode glob grammar; a directory entry that is not valid UTF-8 makes file_list return an error naming it rather than being skipped or matched approximately.
getOpenMSConfigDir follows the source's __unix__ branch, not Rust's unix cfg flag, so macOS resolves to <home>/.OpenMS as the source does.
UTC rather than local time, and the HOSTNAME/COMPUTERNAME environment variable rather than gethostname, in get_unique_name.
Checked Results replace the -1/false/empty-list sentinels; paths are native PathBuf without decorative trailing separators.
native_boundaries: MAX_ENTRIES = 100,000 charged entry visits, counting planning and enumeration visits and not only output rows, so filtering cannot make a traversal cheap
MAX_WORK = 50,000,000 abstract units, charged for path inspection, entry visits, sorting and each character step of a wildcard match, so a pathological pattern is refused rather than run
MAX_BYTES = 64 MiB of conservative logical allocation for paths, copy plans and pattern tokens; file contents are streamed and not charged, with no scientific-data-size cap
MAX_PATH_BYTES = 1 MiB per path or pattern, and an interior NUL is refused, before any filesystem call
MAX_DEPTH = 128 levels for directory creation, recursive copy and recursive removal, checked before anything is created so a rejected make_dir leaves no partial chain
Temporary creation retries at most 100 times, matching the source's own Windows cap; each attempt walks three progressively shorter candidate names and reports a non-length failure at once
get_unique_name refuses a system clock before the Unix epoch, a host name over 255 bytes, and an exhausted counter, none of which the source checks
Param and ParamXML retain their own checked parsing and update budgets; an existing OpenMS.ini without the paramxml feature is an explicit Unsupported rather than a silent fall back to defaults
Ordinary caller-owned context and guard values, and Rust Clone, are not secretly fallible
openmp: None of File.cpp, FileConfig.cpp or FileTemp.cpp carries a #pragma omp. The source's only concurrency is the mutex guarding its temporary-name list and the thread-safe initialisation of its two function-local statics, so there is nothing to parallelise and no performance gap to record; the port is serial and uses no rayon. The concurrency the class test does exercise — simultaneous writable() probes, and a probe racing a real writer — is reproduced natively.
